title: Which limits refuse the next job

blocks.text: A school district funds its summer repair jobs from a capital fund and an asphalt fund, with a fixed number of crew-weeks and one roofing crew. The district's optimizer has chosen this summer's jobs, and every limit has some room left except the roofing crew. The facilities manager asks which limits are really holding the plan back: whole jobs cannot use the last few dollars or crew-weeks, so a limit with room left can still be the reason a job was not added.
Each limit is a `Limit` with a name, how much of it each job uses (`use`; a job not listed uses none) and its cap. A plan is the set of chosen jobs. In `refusals.py`, write:

items: `refusals(limits, plan, candidates)`: for each candidate job, the names of the limits that would be over their cap if that one job were added to the plan, sorted by name. A limit filled exactly to its cap is not over it.
`full_but_not_tight(limits, plan, candidates)`: the names of the limits that have room left at the plan *and* refuse at least one candidate, sorted by name.

blocks.text: With $`u_{\ell,j}`$ what job $`j`$ uses of limit $`\ell`$, $`C_\ell`$ its cap and $`S`$ the plan, write first the test for "adding job $`k`$ breaks limit $`\ell`$" and the test for "limit $`\ell`$ has room at the plan", each as an inequality in $`\sum_{j \in S} u_{\ell,j}`$, $`u_{\ell,k}`$ and $`C_\ell`$. Then code them. Compare amounts with a tolerance of `1e-9`, since uses may be fractional. The tests use their own district; no solver is needed.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from refusals import Limit, full_but_not_tight, refusals

limits = [
    Limit("works_fund", {"bridge": 250, "tunnel": 300, "lights": 80, "kerbs": 40}, 600),
    Limit("crew_months", {"bridge": 5, "tunnel": 6, "lights": 2, "kerbs": 1}, 10),
    Limit("one_big_job", {"bridge": 1, "tunnel": 1}, 1),
]
plan = {"bridge", "lights"}

for job, broken in refusals(limits, plan, ["tunnel", "kerbs"]).items():
    print(f"limits broken by adding {job}:", broken)
print("limits with room that refuse tunnel:", full_but_not_tight(limits, plan, ["tunnel"]))

cases.says: each candidate job is added alone to the plan, and the limits it breaks are listed
a limit the addition fills exactly is not broken
a candidate that breaks several limits lists all of them, sorted by name
a limit with no room left at the plan is binding, not full-but-not-tight
a limit with room that refuses no candidate is not reported

origin.section: On a MILP, a Row With Slack Can Still Be the Row That Blocks

concepts: a row with slack can refuse every whole project that might be added, so the report lists what each row refuses
